How to calculate a discount

Calculating a percentage discount is straightforward once you know the formula. To find the sale price after a percentage discount, multiply the original price by (1 − discount/100). For example, to calculate 20% off £89.99:

  • Savings = £89.99 × 0.20 = £18.00
  • Final price = £89.99 − £18.00 = £71.99
  • Or directly: £89.99 × 0.80 = £71.99

How to find the original price before a discount

If you know the sale price and the discount percentage but need to find the original price, divide the sale price by (1 − discount/100). For example, if an item costs £80 after a 20% discount, the original price was £80 ÷ 0.80 = £100.

Tips for shopping sales and avoiding discount traps

  • Check the original price: Some retailers inflate prices before a sale. Check price history tools to verify the original price was genuine.
  • Compare per unit: A larger pack at a lower percentage discount may be cheaper per unit than a smaller pack with a bigger discount.
  • Stack discounts carefully: If you apply a 20% discount code on top of a 30% sale, you don't get 50% off. You get 30% off, then 20% off the reduced price — which equals 44% total.
  • VAT and tax: In the UK and EU, displayed prices include VAT. In the USA, sales tax is added at checkout — always check whether the discount applies before or after tax.

What is a discount calculator?

A discount calculator instantly shows you the final sale price after a percentage or fixed amount discount, and calculates exactly how much you save. It works for any discount — from a small 5% loyalty reward to a large 70% clearance sale.

Frequently asked questions

How do I calculate 20% off a price?

Multiply the price by 0.80 (1 − 0.20). For example, 20% off £50 = £50 × 0.80 = £40. You save £10. Or use the calculator above — enter £50 and select 20%.

How do I calculate 30% off?

Multiply the price by 0.70. For example, 30% off £120 = £120 × 0.70 = £84. You save £36.

How do I find the original price from a sale price?

Divide the sale price by (1 − discount/100). If an item is £72 after a 10% discount, the original price was £72 ÷ 0.90 = £80.

What is the difference between percentage off and fixed discount?

A percentage discount (e.g. 20% off) scales with the price — the higher the original price, the more you save. A fixed discount (e.g. £10 off) gives the same saving regardless of the original price. Use the toggle above to switch between both types.

If I apply two discounts, do they stack?

No, discounts applied sequentially do not simply add up. A 20% discount followed by a 10% discount gives 28% total off — not 30%. The second discount applies to the already-reduced price.
